comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** On a single bar instance, the freshness text and the low-allowance state machine behave as described. The age wording, the stale threshold (the larger of 30 minutes or two refresh intervals), the missing-timestamp and future-clock handling, notify-once with rearm after recovery, the stale/error skip and the prepaid-balance path all match the PR description. The collectors' Python `isoformat()` timestamps (six-digit fractions, `+00:00` offsets) parse correctly in the Qt 6.11.2 QML engine. The `omarchy-notification-send` argument list matches that helper's parser, with no shell involved.

Two issues are worth addressing: duplicate alerts on multi-monitor setups or after widget re-creation, and a freshness line that reports when the record was written rather than when the usage was measured.

### Alerts repeat once per monitor and after widget re-creation

The bar builds one surface per screen (`shell/plugins/bar/Bar.qml:1197`), and the shell's own comment notes that "a widget that appears once in the layout is still live once per screen" (`Bar.qml:694-695`). Each agents `Panel.qml` instance has its own `Main`, its own `notifiedProviders` map (`Panel.qml:49`) and its own `onProvidersChanged` check (`Panel.qml:355`). Every instance sees the same record write and calls `Quickshell.execDetached` itself. `omarchy-notification-send` sends a new notification on every call, and the notification service does not deduplicate by content.

```text
record write (Claude 8% left)
  ├─ Panel on monitor 1: notifiedProviders = {}  → notify
  └─ Panel on monitor 2: notifiedProviders = {}  → notify   (duplicate)
```

Any re-creation of the widget also starts from an empty map and alerts again while the provider stays low. By source, this happens on a structural layout change, a horizontal/vertical bar switch, a monitor hotplug (for the new screen's copy) and `reloadPlugins()`. Settings-only changes, including editing `lowRemainingPercent`, patch the existing instance and do not reset it. Closing and reopening the popup does not reset it either.

**Impact:** With the agents widget in the default bar layout, a two-monitor desktop gets two identical "allowance low" toasts per crossing. The README's "once per shell session" holds only for a single instance that is never rebuilt.

**Suggested change:** Keep updating `notifiedProviders` in every instance, but send only from one owner, for example the first entry of `bar.moduleWidgets(moduleName)`. The Bluetooth panel already coordinates across monitors this way (`shell/plugins/panels/bluetooth/Panel.qml:428-429`, `:573`). To survive rebuilds, keep the ledger outside widget instances (a shared singleton or a small runtime-state file), or reword the README to "once per crossing while the widget is loaded".

### "Updated" reflects the record write time, not when usage was measured

The new line reads `updatedAt`, which each collector stamps with the current time on every write (`bin/omarchy-agent-usage-claude:889`). For Claude, when the live limits probe fails (offline, HTTP 429, 5xx) and a cached window that has not reset still exists, `collect_limits` returns the cached limits with an empty `usageStatusText` (`omarchy-agent-usage-claude:840-842`). The cache has no age bound other than each window's reset time, so it can be up to 5 hours old for the session window or 7 days for the weekly one.

```text
probe fails → limits = cached (fetched hours or days ago), usageStatusText = ""
record.updatedAt = now → panel: "Updated just now", isStale() = false
```

The alert in this case is normally still accurate: within a window that has not reset, remaining allowance does not grow, so a cached low reading remains low. The freshness line is what misleads, because it does not flag stale data when the endpoint is unreachable or rate limited, the case where a freshness indicator helps most.

Synced-only providers have a related gap. They fall back to `aggregateData.updatedAt` (`shell/plugins/agents/Main.qml:250`), which `aggregateSnapshots` sets to the local merge time (`Main.qml:655`) rather than any snapshot's own `updatedAt` (written at `Main.qml:697`). A remote device that stopped syncing long ago still shows "Updated just now" while the local shell runs. The PR description states that synced-only agents use the aggregate time. The wording can still suggest the remote data is current.

**Impact:** The freshness line can report "Updated just now" over Claude limits that were not re-measured, and over synced-only data of any age.

**Suggested change:** Have the Claude collector emit the probe cache's existing `fetchedAtMs` as a limits timestamp, and use it for the freshness line and alert eligibility when limits are present. Alternatively, set a status when serving cached limits. For synced-only providers, carry the newest `snapshot.updatedAt` per provider through the merge, or word the line so it covers local limits only.

**Optional:** Two smaller behaviors, both traced in source:
- The flag is per provider, not per window. If the session window alerts and then resets while the weekly window is already below threshold, the weekly state is never announced. Keying the flag on provider plus window would cover this.
- `lowRemainingPercent` controls only the toast. The bar icon and limit meters still turn urgent at a fixed 90% used / 10% left (`Panel.qml:45-47`, `:769`), so at `lowRemainingPercent: 25` a toast fires while the bar still looks normal.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of head `51dcb94f`, including the agents plugin, the bar and plugin host code, the usage collectors, `omarchy-notification-send`, and Qt 6.11.2 and Quickshell 0.3.1 source. One sandboxed probe ran the PR's `updatedAgeMs`, `isStale` and `freshnessText` bodies in Qt 6.11.2's non-GUI QML engine. It covered 10 synthetic timestamp cases, including collector-format strings, the 30-minute boundary, future clock skew and a malformed value. All 10 matched their expected results. The repository's node test was not executed. No running shell, multi-monitor session or notification delivery was tested, so the duplicate-alert and re-creation findings rest on source only.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments with targeted follow-up questions, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
